statement: Extend the handoff renderer to emit one slice per role, as a query over tasks grouped by `role`, pulling each task's traced requirements and acceptance criteria with it. No slice is authored or maintained.
title: Generate role slices from the task graph

notes: ⚠️ IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-22 as `lib/stage-scope.mjs`, evaluated by `test/stage-scope.test.mjs`. ACC-0011 and ACC-0012 both pass, so this task's derived status is `accepted` — nothing here is stored, and deleting the tests would move it back (#96, DEC-0012). ⚠️ The vacuity the finding named has MOVED rather than gone: with RBS-0001 retired the live scope is empty, so stage 6's criterion is again satisfiable with nothing checked. That is now a fact about the plan rather than about an author's attention, which is why it is attested `n/a` with a stated basis rather than `satisfied`.
statement: Replace `load-bearing-assertions-at-rung`'s reliance on the optional `loadBearing` flag with a scope derived from the graph — at minimum, every assertion referenced by an active runbook step's `restsOn`.
title: Derive stage 6's scope from graph use rather than a flag

notes: First because everything else needs somewhere to live. ⚠️ Production mode only (DEC-0018): `next dev` is a contributor workflow and never a shipped configuration, so the launch command must not offer it as an option. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-08-27 — A DISCARDED ARCHITECTURE HAD LEAKED IN. The original statement configured `@next/mdx`, an absolute remark-plugin path and Turbopack's config-serialisation constraint. All three belong to FILE-ROUTED MDX, which DEC-0020 explicitly rejected: AST-0030 measured that path compiling the document into the build so an edit changes nothing, which fails REQ-0018. ⚠️ HOW IT GOT IN IS WORTH RECORDING. Those settings came from the PROBE that measured the rejected option. The probe's incidental setup was carried into the plan as though it were the design — the measurement was right and the configuration it needed was the losing alternative's. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-27, and one thing was measured rather than chosen. The routes were first placed at `src/app/` to keep the shell clear of `app/server.mjs`, the walking skeleton DEC-0017 preserves. Next.js ignored them: a root `app/` directory takes precedence over `src/app/`, so the build reported `Route (pages)` with only `/404` and none of the authored files appeared. Moving them to `app/` produced `Route (app)` with `○ /`, and the skeleton is left alone as a colocated non-route file — `server.mjs` is not a `page`, `layout` or `route`, and `.mjs` is not in the default `pageExtensions`. ⚠️ A build that SUCCEEDS while rendering nothing you wrote is the failure mode worth remembering here: `✓ Compiled successfully` was printed both times, and only the route table said which files Next.js had actually found. ⚠️ VERIFIED FROM CLEAN: `.next` removed, `npm run shell:build` from scratch, `next start` bound to 127.0.0.1 only (confirmed against the listening socket, not assumed from the flag), HTTP 200 with the expected body, process terminated and the port confirmed free. `npm audit` reports zero vulnerabilities after adding next, react and react-dom. ⚠️ NOT DONE HERE, on purpose: no MDX integration of any kind, no watcher, no launcher that owns processes, and no planning-content read. The route reads nothing — a convenience read would be the first violation of REQ-0021's confinement, whose own enforcement (TSK-0006, TSK-0015) does not exist yet.
statement: Create the application under `app/` and make `next build` followed by `next start` work on loopback, with a route that responds. No MDX integration of any kind is configured here. The documented one-command launcher is TSK-0013's.
title: Scaffold the Next.js application and its production build/start primitives

notes: ⚠️ The review-status write is a LOCKING capability and DEC-0021 holds those back for individual review before exposure — so it is deliberately NOT part of this task. It arrives with the review action, where it can be examined on its own. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-27. Two adapters, a README stating what is deliberately absent, and six static tests — each falsified before being trusted. ⚠️ THE PROBE ROUTES WERE TEMPORARY AND ARE GONE. Verifying that a Server Component can import the adapters needed a route that imports them; verifying the client refusal needed one that violates the rule. Both were built, measured, and deleted, and the tree was rebuilt clean afterwards. Neither reads planning content — REQ-0021 confines reads to the reader, which does not exist until TSK-0005, so even a throwaway route was written to import without reading. ⚠️ `server-only` was added as a dependency. Next.js implements the guard internally and the package's contents are unused, but the specifier must still RESOLVE, so it is a real dependency rather than a documentation flourish.
statement: Create the adapter modules the shell needs, each beginning with `import 'server-only'` and re-exporting by explicit name or wrapper. Expose only the capabilities the first slice requires. `lib/` itself is not modified and gains no marker, so `bin/` and the test suite keep working under plain Node.
title: Build the `app/server/*` adapter layer over `lib/`

notes: ⚠️ Independent boundaries per read region, not one page-level boundary — the latter makes the whole page the fallback and satisfies DEC-0019 on paper while buying nothing. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-27. Five static tests, each falsified: removing a `connection()`, importing `node:fs`, importing `lib/` directly, and adding a synchronous export each turn the suite red. ⚠️ THE ADAPTER GAINED ONE NAME, deliberately and reviewably: `readStageDocs`, taken from the PUBLISHER rather than written fresh. It already owns what a stage document is — `.md` and `.mdx`, dotfiles ignored, anything else REFUSED — and a second reader in the application would have quietly disagreed with the package about which files count. ⚠️ A PREDICTION WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH (AST-0037): the reader was designed expecting bundling to break `toolRoot()`, and it did not. The design is unchanged, for a narrower reason than the original one, and the comment that asserted the wrong thing was corrected.
statement: Implement the single read path: await `connection()` before each filesystem read, with every read site enclosed by a `<Suspense>` boundary whose fallback names the content it stands in for. Reads reach `lib/` only through the adapter.
title: Build the planning-content reader on the `connection()` + Suspense contract

notes: ⚠️ FOURTH ON PURPOSE, AND THIS IS THE ORDERING DECISION IN THIS PLAN. It could be built last, after there is more to check — and then it would arrive to find a codebase already full of violations, and the pressure would be to weaken the rule rather than fix the code. Built here, it constrains every task after it while the cost of complying is one file at a time. ⚠️ The failing fixtures are not optional polish (ACC-0024): a check nobody has seen fail is a check nobody has seen. ⚠️ SPLIT 2026-08-27. This half needs only the adapter to exist, so it moves earlier and no longer waits on the reader. The read and `<Suspense>` confinement analysis is its sibling. ⚠️ ACC-0024 is satisfied by the PAIR, not by this task alone: both halves must be shown to fail on their own fixtures before the criterion passes. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Three fixtures, eight tests, one lint command, and three defects found before the check was trusted — two by the fixtures (an off-by-one line, and a lazy pattern spanning two statements) and one by running it (a reachability-scoped check that examined almost nothing). ⚠️ A FOURTH DEFECT WAS FOUND IN AN EARLIER TASK'S TEST. ACC-0026's check grepped `lib/` for the string `"server-only"` and went red as soon as a lib module MENTIONED the marker in a comment — which `lib/shell-boundary.mjs` does, since the guard is part of what it explains. It now uses this task's comment-stripping scanner: a check that cannot tell an import from prose is a check that punishes documentation. ⚠️ Fixture adapters deliberately omit `import "server-only"`. Everything under `test/` is collected by `node --test`, and the marker throws outside the RSC compiler (AST-0033), so a fixture carrying it crashed the suite for a reason unrelated to what it tests.
statement: Implement the analysis that runs without executing the application and reports file and line when any module outside `app/server/` imports from `lib/`, whether directly or through a re-export chain that reaches `lib/` indirectly. Ship fixtures containing both shapes and prove the check fails on each.
title: Build the static `app/server` → `lib/` import-boundary check, with failing fixtures

notes: ⚠️ The count rule admits no partial-failure exception. AST-0035 measured the skeleton printing 178 while rendering 177: the total is what turns an incomplete page into a misleading one. ⚠️ SPLIT 2026-08-27 — it was named as visibly oversized when the plan was written, and it was. The totals, the lint surface and located parse failures are its sibling. This half is the navigation spine; that half is the truthfulness rules, and they fail in different ways. ⚠️ Depends on BOTH boundary checks, so every view file written from here on is checked as it lands. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28, and it is the first task whose code the boundary checks actually guard. Before it the lint reported `0 reader consumer(s)` and the two `<Suspense>` detectors had nothing in the real project to examine; it now reports 1 consumer and 6 reachable modules, and both detectors were falsified against `app/page.js` itself. ⚠️ VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION, NOT INFERRED: with `next start` running and nothing rebuilt, changing one attestation on disk moved the displayed current stage from none to `04-requirement-gaps`, and reverting the file moved it back. ⚠️ The smoke check now asserts the READING PANEL's markers as well as the route's. Without that a page whose Suspense boundary never resolved would still pass — the shell ships, the fallback ships, and the content never arrives, which is the streaming form of a build that succeeds while rendering nothing.
statement: Render `/`: the current stage derived from stage definitions and recorded attestations, and all nine stages with their gate state. Status is conveyed by text or icon, never by colour alone. No stored status field is introduced anywhere.
title: Build the project view's stage navigation and derived current stage

notes:
⚠️ Request-time compilation, never file-routed `app/**/page.mdx`: AST-0030 measured that path compiling the document into the build, which satisfies REQ-0017 and silently fails REQ-0018. ⚠️ The compiler and plugin chain are PINNED. Changing the MDX version or adding any remark, rehype or recma plugin reopens security validation before it ships. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Twelve tests against a real `@mdx-js/mdx` compile, each rejection asserting a path AND a line:column, plus a control proving an unguarded compile really does evaluate the expression — without which a rejection and a silent strip would be indistinguishable. Falsified three ways: removing the ESM rule, disabling the unmapped-component check, and replacing rejection with stripping each turn the suite red. ⚠️ THE FORMAT DEFAULT WAS THE FINDING (AST-0038), and it was caught by the production probe rather than by the tests — the mapped component rendered as a bare `

`, which led to discovering that a `.md` path disables MDX parsing and with it every rejection. The test fixture is now deliberately named `.md`, so dropping `format: "mdx"` fails nineteen tests. ⚠️ `components.js` is written with `createElement` rather than JSX so that plain Node can import it. A JSX version would have forced the tests to build their own component map, which would have made them a check on a stub rather than on the vocabulary that ships.
statement: Compile stage documents at request time with `@mdx-js/mdx`, running a remark plugin that FAILS the compile — naming the document path and a line:column — on any ESM import or export, JavaScript expression, JSX attribute expression, JSX spread attribute, or JSX element outside the permitted set. Surface the failure to the operator. Stripping may sit beneath the rejection as defence in depth and may never be the observable behaviour.
title: Build the restricted MDX compiler with rejection diagnostics

notes: At most one stage document per render: DEC-0020's per-request compilation cost is unmeasured, and a view rendering several would multiply an unknown. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. The smoke check now covers `/stage/[stageId]` and requires every region to RESOLVE — criteria, criterion rows, document and review — then rewrites the document in the copy twice: once with a permitted component, asserting it renders, and once with an unmapped one, asserting a located and escaped refusal beside intact criteria. Falsified by removing the catch: the rejection escapes, the region goes blank, and the check fails. ⚠️ ONE THING IS MEASURED AND NOT FIXABLE HERE: an unknown stage returns 200, not 404. `notFound()` runs inside a Suspense child, so the status is committed before the stage turns out not to exist. Validating earlier means reading in the route entry, which the boundary check refuses — so the honest position is that the failure is VISIBLE (Next.js's not-found UI) while the status is not available to make truthful. Recorded as an omission rather than quietly accepted.
statement: Render `/stage/[stageId]`: the stage's exit criteria with their recorded attestations, then the compiled document, then a review panel identifying the artifact under review by id, type, title and current status. Long criterion identifiers wrap rather than overflow.
title: Build the stage view: criteria above the document, artifact-scoped review

notes: ⚠️ Needed because DEC-0022 reloads the page on every content change and every reconnection — at a moment the user did not choose, and without telling them what was lost. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28, and most of the mechanism arrived with TSK-0009 — the stage id is a route segment and the artifact id a query parameter, both read server-side and neither turned into a path. What this task added is the PROOF: fresh-session, reload and control fetches, an invalid-id case, and static checks that no application module reaches for browser storage and no client component holds a selection. ⚠️ THE STATIC CHECKS PASS TRIVIALLY TODAY because there are no client components at all. They are written anyway: the first `"use client"` file is exactly when someone reaches for `useState` to remember which artifact is open, and that is the moment this should fail rather than the moment someone notices a reload lost their place. The count of client components is pinned so it moving is a visible event. ⚠️ DEC-0024 records the accepted 200-for-an-unknown-stage tradeoff, with the reopening condition being a consumer that parses the response rather than reads it.
statement: Encode the selected stage and the selected artifact in the URL so that opening it in a session with no prior client storage restores the same selection. Transient interface state may remain in the client.
title: Put every correctness-critical selection in the URL

notes: ⚠️ A comment-line keepalive is ignored by the client parser (AST-0036) — it keeps the socket warm and leaves the page looking healthy. The heartbeat must be an event a listener can fire on. ⚠️ No event buffer, event id or `Last-Event-ID`: events are hints and never deltas, so a reconnecting client that reloads is exactly caught up. ⚠️ Logging a watcher failure to the server console is explicitly not enough. The operator is looking at a browser. ⚠️ SPLIT 2026-08-27 — also named as visibly oversized, and also correctly. The client listener, watchdog, stale state and reload-on-reconnect are its sibling. The split runs along the wire: this task is what is SENT, that one is what is OBSERVED, and AST-0036 is why those are different problems — a comment keepalive is sent and never observed. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Nine deterministic tests plus a production stream check that observes a heartbeat and a change hint from a real file write without waiting for the stream to end. ⚠️ THE BOUNDARY RULE WAS WIDENED DELIBERATELY, AND ONLY WHERE IT WAS WRONG. `only the reader may import app/server/*` was justified by 'or the read escapes connection()' — a justification that covers the CONTENT adapters and nothing else. A change stream watches rather than reads, so the first non-content adapter would have needed an exemption. Instead each adapter now DECLARES its permitted consumers in `shellBoundaryConfig`, defaulting to the reader alone: the same information stated positively, where a reviewer reads it, still failing closed. A test pins the declaration, and asserts the content adapters are not in it. ⚠️ One drift was caught immediately: the read-boundary test listed its options by hand rather than using the shared config, and went red the moment the lint learned about a new consumer — two descriptions of one rule. It now builds from the config.
statement: Watch the content root and deliver change hints over an event stream. Emit a NAMED heartbeat event carrying data at a fixed interval. When the watcher fails, emit a visible failure signal on the stream or close the stream; logging alone is not permitted.
title: Build the change-stream server: watcher, transport, named heartbeat, failure propagation

notes: ⚠️ THIS IS THE INDIVIDUAL REVIEW DEC-0021 REQUIRES, held out of the adapter task for that reason. It is the first locking capability the shell exposes, and a Server Component may run concurrently in ways a CLI never does — that is what needs examining before the line is added. ⚠️ DEPENDENCY CHANGED 2026-08-27: it waited on the change stream, which coupled the first WRITE path to the streaming work for no reason. The review action needs a view to sit in and a URL to identify an artifact by, and nothing else. Review writing and the stream now proceed independently. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-29 (EVD-0072). The first write the application can perform. ⚠️ THREE STANDING PINS MOVED, AND EACH WAS RESTATED RATHER THAN RELAXED. `no adapter exposes a write` now names the one write that was reviewed and keeps refusing every other, including in the same file. The adapter-consumer map gained the write door and an assertion that it admits exactly one caller. And `no synchronous export` in the reader became `no synchronous export that READS`, with the single exception named, its reason recorded, and a check that it is still what it claims — because `planningRoots` is shared with the write so the page and the write cannot address different directories. ⚠️ THAT LAST CHECK WAS INERT WHEN FIRST WRITTEN AND ONLY FALSIFICATION FOUND IT. A `\b` in the generator became a literal backspace byte in the regex, so it matched nothing and passed with a reader that read. It is the same escaping failure this project has now hit several times, and the only reason it did not ship as a decorative rule is that every new check is made to fail before it is believed. ⚠️ THE END-TO-END TEST IS A REAL POST. Next.js renders a hidden action id so a form works without JavaScript, which means the whole path — markup, dispatch, adapter, lock, atomic write, redirect, re-render — is reachable with `fetch`. It asserts the DISK first and the freshly rendered page second, because a write that persisted while the page kept serving the old value would satisfy every other assertion.
statement: Expose `lib/tools/review-status.mjs` through the adapter and wire the stage view's review panel to it. Updating changes only the named artifact's `reviewStatus`, through the existing lock and atomic write; `lifecycle` and every other artifact are unchanged.
title: Expose the review-status write through the adapter, with individual review

notes: ⚠️ Deliberately AFTER the change stream, because there is no watcher to own until then. ⚠️ The skeleton's create-on-`listen` / close-in-`close()` pattern does not carry: under `next start` there is no server object the application owns. Choosing the binding is this task's work, and DEC-0022 states the obligation without a mechanism for exactly that reason. ⚠️ Verified by observation, not by the absence of an error — the destroy path's own rule. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-08-27 to OWN the documented launcher, which TSK-0003 previously claimed. TSK-0003 scaffolds build and start; a launcher that owns two processes cannot exist until there is a watcher to own, so the command is finished here. ACC-0033 stays traced from both — the scaffold is a necessary condition — but this is where it is SATISFIED. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-29: THERE IS NO SECOND PROCESS, AND THERE NEVER WAS ONE TO OWN. This artifact previously said the launcher owns 'both the application process and the file watcher' and 'terminates the watcher with the application'. The watcher is chokidar, imported dynamically INSIDE the `next start` process and held by the change-stream service in that process's memory. A parent launcher cannot call `changeStream.close()` across that boundary without adding IPC or a shutdown endpoint, and neither is justified for a local-first tool. The old wording described a mechanism that could not be built, which is worse than an unmet obligation: it would have been 'satisfied' by a launcher that called nothing and reported success. ⚠️ WHAT IS TRUE INSTEAD, and all of it is enforceable. The launcher owns ONE child: the `next start` process. The change-stream service owns its watcher and closes it when its last subscriber leaves — already built and tested under TSK-0011. Terminating the application process releases any watcher still open through process teardown, which is the operating system's guarantee rather than the launcher's. `close()` stays what it is: a service and test lifecycle operation, never something the launcher claims to call across a process boundary. ⚠️ THE CLEANUP TEST MUST PROVE THE WATCHER EXISTED FIRST. Without a subscription there is no watcher — the service creates it lazily — so a test that starts the launcher and stops it would observe a clean teardown of nothing and pass vacuously. Opening `/events` and waiting for a named heartbeat is what makes the observation mean something. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-29 (EVD-0073). ⚠️ THE FIRST CLEANUP TEST PASSED AGAINST A LAUNCHER THAT TERMINATED NOTHING, and finding that is most of what this task was worth. Windows reaps the child when the parent exits, so 'the child pid is gone' is true either way; the test now asserts the launcher REPORTED seeing its child exit, which the disabled-termination build fails. ⚠️ A SECOND MEASUREMENT CHANGED THE DESIGN: SIGTERM to the launcher is a hard kill on Windows, so the graceful path never ran and its run directories survived. A stdin stop was added — not for convenience, but because the shutdown guarantee was otherwise unobservable on the platform this project runs on. ⚠️ THE TEST SUITE NEEDED A SHARED LOCK ON `.next`. `node --test` runs files in parallel, and this test and `shell-smoke` both build into and serve from the same directory: first `Another next build process is already running`, then, after a narrow fix that locked only the build, a server dying mid-request because the other test deleted `.next` underneath it. The shared resource was never the build step but the build directory, for as long as anything serves from it. ⚠️ WHAT IS STILL UNEXERCISED: the POSIX shutdown branch (no Linux or macOS host) and a cold install (`node_modules` was present every run).
statement: Provide the single documented command that installs, builds and starts the application in production mode. It launches Next directly as its owned child rather than through a nested npm process, sets and PRINTS an absolute `PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR`, binds loopback explicitly, forwards shutdown to the child, waits for it to exit, and escalates within a bounded time if it does not. Verify cleanup by observation after termination: the child PID is gone, nothing is listening on the port, and no temporary directory the launcher created survives. The cleanup test must first open `/events` and observe a heartbeat, so that a watcher is known to have existed before anything claims it was released.
title: Own the documented one-command launcher, and prove its cleanup

notes: ⚠️ A run in which any measured request did not compile is VOID rather than a pass — the easiest way to hit a compile budget is to cache the document. ⚠️ If the first valid run misses 300 ms by a wide margin, the response is DEC-0020's second alternative — plain markdown for stage documents — not a larger number. That is a PM decision and this task does not take it. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28 (EVD-0071). Six valid runs; ACC-0020 recorded as fail. ⚠️ THIS TASK DOES NOT TAKE THE FALLBACK DECISION, as its own note requires — and the measurement is the reason it should not be taken as written. The budget was missed, but by the read rather than the compiler, so 'plain markdown for stage documents' would cost the rejection contract and buy about 20 ms. That is a PM decision and it now has a different question in front of it: what to do about a per-request read of the whole planning corpus. ⚠️ THE HARNESS IS PERMANENT AND RE-RUNNABLE (`node bin/bench-compile.mjs`), because a number nobody can reproduce is a number nobody can dispute — and this one needs disputing: it is not stable across runs. It prints JSON including every raw sample, so the p95 can be recomputed rather than trusted. ⚠️ IT REFUSES TO REPORT RATHER THAN REPORT SOMETHING FLATTERING. Caching the compiled document produces VOID and a non-zero exit with no timings, falsified by actually memoising it. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-28: the 234-359 ms span was attributed here to reading all 253 artifacts per request. It is not. `readStageDocument` awaits `connection()` and reads the nine stage documents only — `lintProject` is not on its path. What inside that span costs the time is an open question, not a known cost. ⚠️ ACCEPTANCE MOVED 2026-08-28 to ACC-0037, the successor. ACC-0020 stays `fail` and stays readable; this task no longer traces to it, because a task accepted by a retired criterion is accountable to nothing. DEC-0025 records why the plain-Markdown fallback did not fire and QST-0025 carries the unexplained read span.
statement: Measure the 95th-percentile server-side compile-and-render time for the largest stage document under ACC-0020's protocol: pinned environment recorded with the result, timing from read to completed markup, ten discarded warm-up requests, fifty measured serial requests, and per-request verification that compilation occurred. Record the result as evidence.
title: Run the compile benchmark under the pinned protocol

notes: ⚠️ Split from TSK-0006 on 2026-08-27. This half needs the reader to exist, because the rule it enforces is 'reads go through the reader' — there is nothing to be outside of until there is one. ⚠️ ACC-0024 is satisfied by the PAIR with TSK-0006, and it holds for each half separately: a check nobody has seen fail is a check nobody has seen. ⚠️ Both halves land before any view work. Built afterwards they would arrive to a codebase already full of violations, and the pressure would be to weaken the rule rather than fix the code. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Four detectors, six fixtures, eleven tests, and three defects found before anything was trusted — two in the fixtures (import paths that climbed out of the app directory, so the ALLOWED case reported clean because nothing resolved) and one in the analyser (two template-literal regexes that lost a backslash level, leaving a detector unable to fire at all). ⚠️ THE SUSPENSE DETECTORS HAVE NOTHING TO CHECK IN THE REAL APPLICATION YET — the lint reports `0 reader consumer(s)`, because no view imports the reader until TSK-0007. That is stated rather than left for someone to discover: today they are proven by fixtures and by temporary real-code violations, and they begin covering real code with the first view.
statement: Implement the analysis that runs without executing the application and reports file and line for a planning-content filesystem read performed anywhere other than the reader, and for a read site not enclosed by a `<Suspense>` boundary. Ship fixtures containing both violations and prove the check fails on each.
title: Build the static planning-read and `<Suspense>` confinement check, with failing fixtures

notes: ⚠️ Split from TSK-0007 on 2026-08-27, because the truthfulness rules are where this view fails SILENTLY and they deserve their own review rather than riding along with the navigation. ⚠️ THE COUNT RULE ADMITS NO PARTIAL-FAILURE EXCEPTION. AST-0035 measured the skeleton printing 178 while rendering 177: the total is what turns an incomplete page into a misleading one, because an operator reading it has been told the missing thing is present. ⚠️ ACC-0014 is evaluated against a FIXTURE of known composition, never against the page — the page renders totals rather than entries, so counting what it shows would compare a number with itself. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Nine tests: an offline fixture with a declared composition, a corrupt-one case, a control proving a file count and a parsed count genuinely differ, static checks that the panel re-judges nothing, and a production sequence that corrupts a file while serving, requires the total to fall by one and the located error to appear, then restores it and requires both to recover — with no rebuild and no restart. ⚠️ FALSIFIED WITH A CONSTANT TOTAL AND WITH SUPPRESSED ERROR OUTPUT, as required, and each failed only its own assertion. That separation is the point: a single check covering both would let a page that counts correctly but hides failures pass on the strength of its arithmetic. ⚠️ THE READER HAD THE SAME DEFECT THE SKELETON DID. `artifactCount` was `lint.records.length` — a FILE count — since TSK-0005. It was never displayed, so nothing had caught it; writing the component that would have displayed it is what did.
statement: Add to `/`: artifact totals for each type, lint findings surfaced rather than re-judged, and reporting for a file that fails to parse — named with its path and a position, omitted from the page, and subtracted from its type's total. No rendered total may include an artifact the page did not render.
title: Build the project view's artifact totals, lint surface and located parse failures

notes: ⚠️ Split from TSK-0011 on 2026-08-27. This is the half REQ-0018's second clause actually lands on. AST-0034 measured the skeleton's idle and dead streams as byte-identical and no client-side cleverness recovers a difference that was never transmitted — but equally, a heartbeat nothing listens for is not visibility either, so neither half is sufficient alone. ⚠️ Reload on reconnection is what removes the work: events are hints and never deltas (#73), so a reconnecting client that reloads is exactly caught up and no replay machinery is needed. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Thirteen deterministic tests plus a production check that the client half actually reaches the browser. ⚠️ ACC-0029 AND ACC-0030 REMAIN NOT-EVALUATED, DELIBERATELY. No browser was available, so a visibly stale page within the watchdog window and a reconnection that recovers a missed change have not been seen happening. They are the two criteria a reasonable person would most want ticked, which is precisely why they are not. ⚠️ THE BOUNDARY CHECK RELOCATED THE CODE. `lib/stream-watchdog.mjs` was refused by `lint:shell` on its first run; `app/server/*` was impossible because `server-only` throws in a client component. `app/_stream/logic.js` is neither tool nor adapter, which is what a client component needs — the same shape `app/_mdx/reject-js.js` already had. ⚠️ THE SMOKE CHECK LOOKS PAST THE HTML. Server-rendered markup for a client component is identical whether or not the script ships, so the check fetches every script the page loads and requires one to contain the component's own text. Falsified with a static stand-in that passes the markup assertions and fails only that one.

statement: Establish, against the pinned runtime and with nothing of Kiln's involved, what Pi's interactive `/login` step does: whether it can be launched with exclusive terminal ownership, what its exit conveys and whether authentication must be rediscovered afterwards rather than inferred from the exit code, and what happens when it is invoked with no TTY — refusal, error, or an indefinite wait. notes: ⚠️ MANUAL AND OUTSIDE CI BY DECISION, not by omission. Automating it would require a real subscription credential in CI, which REQ-0024 forbids. ⚠️ DO NOT FABRICATE THE CREDENTIAL. Writing a canonical-shaped OAuth record into `auth.json` proves the shape round-trips and nothing about whether a subscription authenticates; the spike already did exactly that and the model stayed unavailable, which was a fact about provider composition rather than about OAuth. ⚠️ THE REVOCATION CONTROL IS THE HALF THAT CARRIES THE RESULT. Without it a model that was already available for an unrelated reason reads as a successful login. ⚠️ UNTIL THIS RUNS, no criterion and no section of the specification may state the OAuth route as verified — 'supported' is what the documentation may say.

Retain a sanitized single-instance evidence record — no token, header, credential-derived value, username or home path — and label it as manual and account-bound so it is never mistaken for a suite result.
